thread:
camille: Heads-up — after landing the NF4/FP4 calibration sweep in canary, we see a sustained throughput drop on a subset of model shards. Not catastrophic but enough to fail SLOs for some routes.

ravi: Which routes/seq-lens? any kernel change logs?

camille: Mainly chat endpoints with seq_len ~512; QPS steady but p95 token latency up ~22% and aggregate tokens/sec down ~18%. Kernel selection trace shows a switch to the int4-fused attention path for some shards.

diana: hmm. Could calibration have nudged quant params so the scheduler picks different kernels (faster numerically but worse memory locality)? Did we get KV cache housekeeping bloat?

camille: Attaching snippet from canary profiler (trimmed):
```
shard=12 seq_bucket=512 kernel=attn_int4_fused cpu% 38 -> 55 (post-calib)
kv_cache_hits 92% -> 67%
alloc_slab_frag 12% -> 48%
tokens/sec 12.4k -> 10.1k
```

matt: alloc_slab_frag spike is suspicious — could be calibration changing tensor shapes or quant layout causing more small allocations and poorer reuse. Any changes to batching heuristics at rollout time?

camille: No batching code changed. We did enable aggressive per-layer clamp tuning for NF4 which changes per-layer scale placement. Perf-bot logged kernel preference updates at 1853023490 for the affected model.

perf-bot: kernel-preferences-updated: model=redwood-v2-neo4bit canary=on reason=calibration_tuning

ravi: Two quick hypotheses: 1) the fused int4 kernel uses a different memory pattern that increases KV cache fragmentation and prevents reuse, 2) fallback logic misrouted some long-context requests to CPU path intermittently. Can we repro on a single node with a loadgen?

diana: I spun up a repro instance with the same calib weights + standard traffic profile. Repro steps:
1) start canary image (tag nf4-calib-2026-03-10)
2) run loadgen profile chat-512 for 10m (ramp 60s)
3) collect /metrics and heap snapshots every 60s

Result: tokens/sec dropped ~17% after ~90s, slab fragmentation rose in step. Heap snapshots show many ~8KB small allocations in kv slab.

matt: That aligns. Maybe the quant tuning changed per-head or per-mlp buffer sizes so we now have more small activations stored in KV. Two mitigations: a) adjust slab allocator to prefer larger chunk coalescing for kv, b) pin kernel choices to the previous kernel for 512 bucket until we fix allocator.

camille: For immediate mitigation I propose canary rollback to previous kernel prefs and deploy a slab-defrag hotfix to staging. Also start an A/B of disabling the per-layer clamp for a small traffic % to confirm cause.

ravi: +1. I'll open an ops rollout ticket and add a canary flag to pin kernel. Can someone capture the exact kernel hash we want to pin to?

camille: Pinned to kernel hash ab12f4c (pre-calib fused-attn fallback). I'll paste the kernel map and a perf diff later.

diana: Action list:
- ravi: pin kernel in canary (rollback) and create rollback PR (ETA 30m)
- matt: prototype slab-defrag change (staging test)
- camille: collect more heap snapshots + run allocation flame graphs across shards (I have preliminary traces)
- perf-bot: run nightly regression with and without per-layer clamp to see global effect

matt: One more note — also check GPU memory fragmentation (nvidia-smi metrics). If nv driver alloc churn is high it amplifies perf hits.

camille: Good call. I see a small bump in NV alloc churn correlating with the time tokens/sec drops. OK let's coordinate on the rollback first. I'll post the kernel map and flamegraphs here in 10m. :thumbsup:
